transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I guess I'm here because of dispatch. Dispatch and compliance, they’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And they make these little comments on the radio. We use those heavy two-way radios in the cabs, you know? The ones with the thick coiled cords. I actually had to get my cord replaced a few weeks ago because it kept catching on the seat adjustment lever. The seats in those vehicles are just terrible for your lower back, honestly. I tried bringing in this lumbar pillow my sister got me for Christmas—she always buys me practical gifts, which is fine, but sometimes you just want a gift card or something, right? But... anyway, even when people say it’s just normal oversight, the tracking I mean, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. They're definitely watching and reporting on me.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that dispatch and certain drivers are tracking and reporting on you?

Well, it’s been about... I’d say for the past two months, the tracking through the computer system and those radio comments have felt really clear to me. Two months ago exactly, actually, because that was right around the time I had to get my windshield wipers replaced. The ones the company puts on the vehicles are so cheap, they just smear the rain everywhere, you know? I had to go down to the auto parts store on 4th street to buy the good silicone ones myself. 

The guy at the register kept trying to upsell me on this premium orange washer fluid—the kind that supposedly melts ice?—but honestly, the cheap blue stuff works just fine if you just let your defroster warm up first. My uncle used to swear by the blue stuff, and he drove long-haul trucks for thirty years before he retired down to Florida. The humidity down there is just awful for his joints, though, he complains about it every time he calls. But, um... yeah. About two months of the computer and radio stuff being really obvious.
Over these past two months, have you also noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the flip side, unusually energetic or elated—that lasted for days at a time?

Um, no, not really. I haven't felt sad or hopeless or... anything like that. And I'm not unusually energetic either. I mean, I do drink a lot of coffee to stay awake during my routes, so sometimes I get a little jittery, but that's just the caffeine. 

There's this little drive-thru coffee hut on Route 9 that I always stop at, and the girl who works the morning shift makes the best iced Americanos. But they just raised their prices again! It's like, almost six dollars for a medium now. Can you believe that? My mom says I should just buy a thermos and make it at home to save money, but those stainless steel thermoses always make the coffee taste like metal to me. I tried soaking one in baking soda like the internet said to get the metallic smell out, but it didn't really help. It just made this gritty paste in the sink that took forever to scrub out. So I just pay the six dollars, it's easier. But... yeah, no, my mood is just normal, I guess. I haven't noticed any changes like that.
Aside from the comments you hear over the radio, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to notice?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't seen anything, and I don't hear voices or anything like that, just what comes through the dispatch radio. My hearing is actually really sharp, though. I actually had to start wearing those little foam earplugs to sleep because the guy in the apartment above me got a dog, and it just paces all night long. Click, click, click on the hardwood. 

The landlord sent out this memo saying everyone in the building has to have rugs covering eighty percent of the floor, but he clearly hasn't enforced it upstairs. Which, I mean, to be fair, rugs are ridiculously expensive right now. I was at the home goods store on Sunday looking for just a simple runner for my hallway, and they wanted like ninety dollars for this ugly mustard yellow one. Who even buys mustard yellow? It shows every single speck of dirt. Especially with all the salt they put on the roads around here in the winter. You track that inside and it just ruins everything, it leaves those crusty white stains. The salt actually completely rusted out the muffler on my last personal car. The mechanic told me it wasn't even worth fixing, because the whole undercarriage was just eaten away... so, yeah, just the radio comments.
Do you have any medical conditions—like thyroid problems, seizures, or head injuries—or do you use any recreational drugs or drink alcohol regularly?

Um, no, no medical conditions. My thyroid is fine, no seizures or anything. And I don't really drink or do drugs. I mean, I'll have a beer sometimes if I'm at a barbecue, but I actually haven't been to a barbecue since my cousin's graduation party last summer. 

They had this huge spread, like brisket and ribs, but the guy they hired to cater it showed up two hours late. He said his van broke down on the interstate, but honestly, I think he just double-booked himself because he kept checking his phone the whole time he was setting up the chafing dishes. Those chafing dishes are so dangerous, too. You know the little cans of fuel they put under them? My aunt knocked one over at a wedding once, and it set the tablecloth on fire. It was a complete disaster. The bride was crying, the fire alarm went off, and the sprinklers ruined the cake. It was a red velvet cake, too, which is my favorite. But they use so much food coloring in red velvet, it's probably not even good for you. I read an article that said red dye 40 can cause hyperactivity in kids. But, um... yeah, no medical problems, and I don't use drugs.
Over these past two months, has your ability to do your job or keep up with your usual daily activities and relationships changed at all because of these concerns about being watched?

Um, well... yeah, it has, I guess. I've fallen really behind on my route reports at work. And my instructions over the dispatch have gotten, um, a little confusing, I guess, because some of the drivers have been complaining to management about it. It's just hard to focus when I know they're listening to me. 

And at home, it's been tough, too. My husband has had to take over basically everything—making meals, taking phone calls, doing all the basic planning, because I'm just... I'm not keeping up with it. He made spaghetti last night, actually, but he always forgets to salt the pasta water. You really have to salt the water until it tastes like the sea, that's what all the chefs on TV say. I watch a lot of those cooking competition shows when I can't sleep. The ones where they give them a basket of weird ingredients like gummy bears and octopus and tell them to make an appetizer in twenty minutes. I don't know how they do it. I panic if I just have to figure out what to make with chicken breasts and broccoli. Chicken breasts dry out so fast if you're not careful. My mom used to bake them for like an hour until they were basically leather, and we had to choke them down with so much ketchup. Ketchup has a lot of hidden sugar in it, though. You'd be surprised. But, um... yeah, so my husband has been doing all the cooking and stuff because I've just been having a hard time keeping up with everything.

Before these past two months when things became really clear, did you notice any smaller signs—like feeling suspicious, on edge, or that something was 'off' with coworkers or dispatch—going back further, even if they weren't as strong?

Um, well, yeah, I guess it's been building for a while now. Probably for about eight months, actually, ever since they put me in that temporary dispatch lead role. 

That whole promotion process was such a mess, honestly. They said it was temporary, but then the guy who was supposed to come back from medical leave ended up moving to Florida. Florida is so humid, I don't know how anyone lives there. My grandparents used to have a timeshare in Orlando, and we went down there once in August. The air was so thick you could practically drink it, and the mosquitoes were the size of quarters. I got bit right on the ankle, and it swelled up so big I couldn't even put my sneaker on. I had to wear these cheap flip-flops we bought at a gas station for the rest of the trip. And gas station flip-flops are the worst, they have that little plastic piece that goes between your toes and it just rubs and rubs until you get a blister. Blisters take forever to heal, too, especially on your feet because you're always walking on them. You have to use those special hydrocolloid bandages, but they're so expensive. Everything at the pharmacy is expensive now. I went in just to buy some toothpaste the other day and it was almost eight dollars. For toothpaste! It's ridiculous. But, um... yeah, about eight months ago, when I got that temporary lead job, that's when things started feeling off.

Over these past several months, have people close to you—like your husband—mentioned that your speech seems harder to follow, or that you've become more withdrawn, flat, or less emotionally expressive than before?

Um, I guess my husband has said I'm... different. I don't know about flat, but I just don't have the energy for things I used to do. Like, I used to sing with this community choir, and we'd always host the softball team at our house after games, but I just don't feel like doing any of that anymore. 

Softball is actually really hard on your knees, you know? Especially if you play catcher. My cousin played catcher in high school, and she had to have two surgeries by the time she was twenty. The physical therapy she had to do was intense. They made her do these exercises with those giant rubber bands, the resistance bands. I bought a set of those once during the pandemic when all the gyms were closed, but they just sat in the box. The rubber always smells so weird, like tires or something. And speaking of tires, I really need to get my car's alignment checked. It pulls to the right every time I get on the highway. Highways are so stressful anyway, people drive like maniacs. But, um... yeah, most days after my shift, I just end up sitting at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there. I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do anything else, really. I just... sit.
Even in moments when you're not thinking about dispatch or being watched—like on a day off—do you still find yourself lacking energy or motivation to do things you used to enjoy?

Um, yeah... even on my days off, I just... I don't know. Like I said before, I just don't feel like doing the choir anymore, or having the softball team over. It's just too much. Even when I'm not thinking about work, I'll just sit at the kitchen table. My planner will be open, and I just sit there. I can't make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or... anything. 

Planners are supposed to help you stay organized, but I think they just make me feel worse. I bought this really nice one at the beginning of the year, it has a leather cover and all these different colored tabs for the months. I used to love color-coding things. My favorite pens were those gel ones, the ones that smell like fruit? I had a cherry one that I used so much the ink ran out in like two weeks. Cherry is the best flavor for anything, really. Cherry candy, cherry soda... my husband bought black cherry soda last week, but it's not the same. It tastes too much like cough syrup. I had this awful cough when I was a kid, it lasted for a whole month, and my mom made me take this thick, red medicine that tasted exactly like that soda. It was awful. But, um... yeah, I just sit at the table with the planner open and I just can't bring myself to do anything.

No mood episode or hallucinations reported, keeping F22 and F20.81 as differential, though F22 typically shows less functional impairment than seen here.

doctor.intent: Determine total duration of symptoms including any prodromal phase, to distinguish schizophreniform disorder (F20.81, <6 months) from schizophrenia (F22, >6 months)
doctor.question: Before these past two months when things became really clear, did you notice any smaller signs—like feeling suspicious, on edge, or that something was 'off' with coworkers or dispatch—going back further, even if they weren't as strong?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been building for about 8 months, since I was put in the temporary dispatch lead role.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the symptoms prior to the 2-month period of psychotic symptoms, specifically asking if smaller signs were noticed going back further. This maps to the 'Duration' key, which indicates the symptoms have been building for 8 months since she was put in the temporary dispatch lead role.

patient.answer:
Um, well, yeah, I guess it's been building for a while now. Probably for about eight months, actually, ever since they put me in that temporary dispatch lead role. 

That whole promotion process was such a mess, honestly. They said it was temporary, but then the guy who was supposed to come back from medical leave ended up moving to Florida. Florida is so humid, I don't know how anyone lives there. My grandparents used to have a timeshare in Orlando, and we went down there once in August. The air was so thick you could practically drink it, and the mosquitoes were the size of quarters. I got bit right on the ankle, and it swelled up so big I couldn't even put my sneaker on. I had to wear these cheap flip-flops we bought at a gas station for the rest of the trip. And gas station flip-flops are the worst, they have that little plastic piece that goes between your toes and it just rubs and rubs until you get a blister. Blisters take forever to heal, too, especially on your feet because you're always walking on them. You have to use those special hydrocolloid bandages, but they're so expensive. Everything at the pharmacy is expensive now. I went in just to buy some toothpaste the other day and it was almost eight dollars. For toothpaste! It's ridiculous. But, um... yeah, about eight months ago, when I got that temporary lead job, that's when things started feeling off.

inference.note: Symptom duration now clarified as ~8 months (exceeding the 1-6 month window for schizophreniform disorder) with clear functional decline at work and home, making chronic schizophrenia (F20.9) more likely than F20.81. Delusional disorder (F22) remains possible given the encapsulated, non-bizarre persecutory/referential beliefs without hallucinations, though the degree of functional impairment argues against a pure delusional disorder.

doctor.intent: Assess for disorganized speech/behavior or negative symptoms (e.g., social withdrawal, blunted affect) beyond the circumscribed persecutory beliefs, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder
doctor.question: Over these past several months, have people close to you—like your husband—mentioned that your speech seems harder to follow, or that you've become more withdrawn, flat, or less emotionally expressive than before?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about becoming withdrawn, flat, or less emotionally expressive, which directly corresponds to Negative Symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um, I guess my husband has said I'm... different. I don't know about flat, but I just don't have the energy for things I used to do. Like, I used to sing with this community choir, and we'd always host the softball team at our house after games, but I just don't feel like doing any of that anymore. 

Softball is actually really hard on your knees, you know? Especially if you play catcher. My cousin played catcher in high school, and she had to have two surgeries by the time she was twenty. The physical therapy she had to do was intense. They made her do these exercises with those giant rubber bands, the resistance bands. I bought a set of those once during the pandemic when all the gyms were closed, but they just sat in the box. The rubber always smells so weird, like tires or something. And speaking of tires, I really need to get my car's alignment checked. It pulls to the right every time I get on the highway. Highways are so stressful anyway, people drive like maniacs. But, um... yeah, most days after my shift, I just end up sitting at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there. I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do anything else, really. I just... sit.

inference.note: Added evidence of negative symptoms (anergia, avolition, reduced speech, withdrawal) and marked functional decline across multiple domains, along with tangential speech patterns, which favor schizophrenia (F20.9) over isolated delusional disorder (F22), though F22 remains possible given the encapsulated persecutory theme.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's loss of interest, low energy, and withdrawal occur even in situations unrelated to the surveillance concerns (suggesting broader negative symptoms of schizophrenia) or only when the surveillance beliefs are triggered (suggesting a more circumscribed delusional disorder)
doctor.question: Even in moments when you're not thinking about dispatch or being watched—like on a day off—do you still find yourself lacking energy or motivation to do things you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a lack of energy or motivation to do things previously enjoyed, which directly relates to the negative symptoms profile (diminished motivation, social interest, emotions).

patient.answer:
Um, yeah... even on my days off, I just... I don't know. Like I said before, I just don't feel like doing the choir anymore, or having the softball team over. It's just too much. Even when I'm not thinking about work, I'll just sit at the kitchen table. My planner will be open, and I just sit there. I can't make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or... anything. 

Planners are supposed to help you stay organized, but I think they just make me feel worse. I bought this really nice one at the beginning of the year, it has a leather cover and all these different colored tabs for the months. I used to love color-coding things. My favorite pens were those gel ones, the ones that smell like fruit? I had a cherry one that I used so much the ink ran out in like two weeks. Cherry is the best flavor for anything, really. Cherry candy, cherry soda... my husband bought black cherry soda last week, but it's not the same. It tastes too much like cough syrup. I had this awful cough when I was a kid, it lasted for a whole month, and my mom made me take this thick, red medicine that tasted exactly like that soda. It was awful. But, um... yeah, I just sit at the table with the planner open and I just can't bring myself to do anything.

inference.note: The patient endorses significant negative symptoms (anhedonia, avolition, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities like choir and socializing) present even apart from persecutory beliefs, plus marked functional decline in both work and home domains over ~8 months, and persistently tangential/circumstantial speech throughout the interview. This combination of positive symptoms (persecutory delusions, possibly non-bizarre auditory misinterpretation via radio), negative symptoms, and functional decline for more than 6 months is more consistent with schizophrenia than delusional disorder, which requires preserved functioning and absence of prominent negative/disorganized features. No mood episode was identified, arguing against a mood or schizoaffective disorder.
